tool_input.command: find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -type d -name "*guren*" -print 2>/dev/null; echo "---"; find / -type d -iname "core" -path "*guren*" 2>/dev/null | grep -v node_modules/.cache | head -20

result: I added Japanese localization for the login and registration pages. Changes: `src/app.ts` now declares `ja` as a supported locale alongside `en` (the framework's existing `detectLocaleMiddleware`/`Accept-Language` parsing handles the ja/ja-JP/quality-value matching automatically, so no custom detection code was needed); the English copy of `Login.tsx`/`Register.tsx` moved out of the components into a new `lang/en/auth.json` namespace (keys unchanged from the current wording), a mirrored `lang/ja/auth.json` was added with the requested Japanese strings, and `lang/ja/messages.json` was added with the translated `welcome` key (placeholder preserved); both page components now call `useTranslation()` from `@guren/inertia-client` and render every label/heading/button/link through `t('auth.login.*')` / `t('auth.register.*')`. Regenerated `.guren/translations.gen.ts` via `bun run codegen` and confirmed `guren check --i18n` reports full key parity between `en` and `ja`. Added `tests/Auth.test.ts`, which boots the real app and exercises `/login` and `/register` under various `Accept-Language` headers (missing, ja-first browser header, English-outranks-Japanese, unsupported language) asserting the rendered HTML contains the correct-language strings. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (7/7).
